chunks: And from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him in Makkah: 'I have a request.' He said: 'Meet me in Makkah.' So I met him and said: 'O son of Allah's Messenger, I have a request.' He said: 'Meet me in Mina.' So I met him in Mina and said: 'O son of Allah's Messenger, I have a request.' He said: 'Present your request.' I said: 'O son of Allah's Messenger, I committed a sin that is between me and Allah, which no one else knows of, and I hold you in too high esteem to reveal it before you.' He said: 'On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will manifest Himself to His believing servant and make him stand accountable for his sins one by one, then He will pardon them for him. Neither an archangel nor a prophet ever sent will know of this. And in another tradition: He will conceal from him his sins that he dislikes to be made aware of, then He will say to his evil deeds: Become good deeds. And that is the word of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: "So those are they of whom Allah changes their evil deeds to good ones."'

key_terms.ذَنْبًا ذَنْبًا: Sin by sin / One by one

ai.seo_question: How does Allah forgive individual sins on the Day of Resurrection without others knowing?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (a.s.) elucidates the unique honor of private accountability, where Allah personally reveals the believer's hidden sins to him alone, shielding them from the gaze of angels and prophets. This divine concealment allows for a direct transformation of those specific sins into good deeds, illustrating the concept of *tabdil al-sayyi'at bi al-hasanat* (converting bad deeds to good) as a special grace for the faithful. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on Allah's intimate knowledge and mercy, distinguishing the believer's final reckoning from the general public accounting.
